Refs #56

## Summary

The live Dictation, wired end to end: hold fn, local Parakeet, text at the cursor.

```text
main.swift (before AppKit)
  AppDelegate.startSystem
    LexiconSystem.live        tap first; one InputClock
    Task.detached system.run
      conductor.follow(keyboard.commands)
      conductor.recover(); history.sweepAudio
      recorder.prepare(mic)
      speech.warmUp(prefs)
      preferences.changes -> speech.preferencesChanged
applicationDidFinishLaunching
  indicator.follow(conductor.events(), recorder.levels)
  will-sleep -> conductor.systemWillSleep
applicationShouldTerminate -> .terminateLater until conductor.idle()
```

The Reviewer's must-fix from #123:

```diff
-case dictationStopped(at:)
+case dictationStopped(DictationID, at:)   // minted at fn-down, on every command
-keyboard.endDictation()
+keyboard.systemWillSleep()               // a release, on the same ordered stream
+guard captureEnd == nil else { log "fn-down dropped" }
```

Also: `Recorder.levels` for the pill; a lag and engine line per Dictation (`scripts/lag-report.sh` gives p50/p95); `lexicon-eval` loads Parakeet first; the `dictate` hook takes fixtures only; `install-app.sh` keeps `<app>.old`.

## Evidence

- **Must-fix, before:** `sleepWithTheNextPressStillQueuedKeepsThatDictation` and `aCommandForAnotherPressNeverEndsTheRecording` failed with the ids carried but ignored: the second Dictation's row was nil (deleted by the lone tap). **After:** pass.
- `everyPressEndsBeforeTheNextBeginsWhateverTheInputs`: 2,000 seeded random input sequences through the real `FnGesture`. The old silent reset fails it with 22,184 issues.
- `backToBackDictationsTypeInTheOrderTheyWereSpoken`: the first Dictation's text comes last and still types first. It fails with `insertTurn` removed.
- **Live** ([Live checks comment](https://github.com/jparker2006/lexicon/issues/56#issuecomment-6109845672), release builds, 469462f and 0d3adf5; Wi-Fi on, 8,660 zero-socket samples):
  - Text lands at the cursor in Claude desktop, ChatGPT Codex, TextEdit and Terminal.
  - 48 Dictations: lag p50 159 ms, p95 351 ms, max 743 ms (provisional: load average 5 to 28). Start gap p50 36 ms, p95 58 ms.
  - Launch to fn: 42 to 80 ms. Back-to-back in order 5 of 5. Lone taps leave nothing. Crash recovery works. Quit takes 64 to 418 ms and SIGTERM 63 ms on 0d3adf5.
  - 1 of 48 was not inserted, reason `typedSince`: a key or click came between fn-up and the paste, so the late-text rule held it for paste-last, as designed.
- **Live, found and fixed:**
  - SIGTERM hung on 469462f. The SIGTERM handler on the main queue called `terminate`, whose `.terminateLater` reply needs the main queue: a deadlock. A standalone AppKit repro hangs before the fix and exits after it.
  - Once, after the first paste on a fresh install, the fn tap went silent with no disabled event. It did not come back on 0d3adf5. A 2 s check now re-enables a silently disabled tap and logs it.
- **Size:** bundle 7.38 MB (budget 12). The binary is 7.7 MB; the linker map puts FluidAudio at 4.74 MB of 6.31 MB of symbols, leaving about 1.6 MB of ours (budget 4).
- `scripts/check.sh` at bf7c0b9: everything passes except the 5 CodeTerms FSEvents tests, which fail on this Mac on a clean `origin/main` too (load). CI is the gate. lexicon-eval on the public fixtures: no worse verdicts.
- Test set `lexicon-eval` not run: no baselines yet (#51 open), and it would load the Mac during Jake's live run. Speech text is unchanged; only when the model loads moved.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way.

**Blast Radius:** live-path

- **Idle memory:** 24 MB 11 minutes after a Dictation with History unopened, inside the 30 MB budget ([re-check](https://github.com/jparker2006/lexicon/issues/56#issuecomment-6110131522)). The unload logged exactly 10:00 after the Dictation. The first run's 36 MB included the History window, which holds about 3.5 MiB after closing (#112), and Core ML keeps about 9 MB after unload (probe).
- **Launch:** on one fresh install the status item came up at 1,639 ms, after the 868 ms model load (fn working at 763 ms). Relaunches bring fn up in 42 to 80 ms. Watch whether the launch warm-up delays the icon.
- **Upgrading from 469462f:** that build's SIGTERM hang makes an install wait up to 21 min. Jake's daily copy never ran it.
- **Merged with #66 and #71:** the Lexicon page edits the system's Lexicon, and the 2 s load wait now sits on the race's local side, so with a cloud model the cloud can still win.

- fn now types for real. Wrong-place text is guarded by `InsertGuard` on every insert (#54).
- The 2 s load wait also covers recovery and waiting retries: during a first-launch compile they go waiting again and retry in 30 s. Proposed deviation, recorded in `docs/architecture.md`.
- Quit hangs while a recording never ends (a lost fn-up) until the 20-minute cap lands (#58).
- Not wired, by design: Fixes, Jev (no Jev call on any Dictation), the inbox, `CodeTerms.start()`.
- Later: recovery's unreadable-audio retry loops every 30 s (#59); a live job waits behind a running background one; a settings change re-arms the 10-minute linger; the lost-fn-up `flagsState` check and the Sounds 256-frame buffer are unmeasured.
- Merge order: none pending in these files.

## Install

The local model must be installed (`scripts/install-model.sh`, already done on this Mac). The first launch of each new build compiles it for about 25 s in the background. Code only otherwise.

Check: hold fn in Claude desktop, say a sentence, let go: the text lands at the cursor.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

comments.body:
Verdict: merge with notes, once Live checks passes the head under review and CI is green.

Reviewed `469462f` with three critics (wiring with never-lose and inserting text, the gesture with levels and real-time safety, and the shell with privacy and install), plus `0d3adf5`. M0 critical path: I read `LexiconSystem.swift` in full and the fix commit.

What holds:
- Launch: the fn tap starts first, one `InputClock` is shared by the tap and `TargetApp`, the key loop runs before recovery, and recovery touches only an earlier run's rows and files. Then the retention sweep, mic prepare and the model warm-up.
- #123's must-fix: fn-down mints a `DictationID`, every command carries it, and `endCapture` ignores other ids, so a press can only end or discard its own capture. Sleep is fed through the recognizer in the same ordered stream. 2,000 seeded random sequences pass, where the old reset fails with 22,184 issues.
- Never lose and inserting: back-to-back Dictations type in spoken order. A model still loading 2 s after fn-up makes the Dictation wait and retry untyped. Quit waits for a recording to end and for in-flight runs (30 s cap), and can't cut a Cmd-V.
- Real time: RMS levels are computed on the writer queue once per chunk, the sink block is unchanged, and observers are `bufferingNewest(1)`. A level is one Float, so no samples leave the capture.
- Privacy: no network path from a live Dictation (speech cloud nil, Cleanup `.off`, Jev and Fixes nil). Keys come from the Keychain. New logs hold ids, status, lag and model only. `lag-report.sh` prints aggregates only. The test hooks stay `#if DEBUG` and are gated to dev.
- `0d3adf5`: SIGTERM no longer hangs quit, since `terminate` runs as a run-loop block outside the handler (before, `install.sh` would have waited out its 21-minute cap). A 2 s watchdog re-enables a tap macOS turned off without notice.

No blockers. Notes are on the Later list (https://github.com/jparker2006/lexicon/issues/36#issuecomment-6106073553). The two to do soon: the AirPods check on an idle prepared mic, and have quit wait for the clipboard restore.

**Before I merge:** a `Live checks:` comment on #56 for the PR's head (four apps, back-to-back, launch to fn, idle memory, crash recovery), and green CI on that head.

Hold (Reviewer): don't merge yet. Live checks' results for `0d3adf5` on #56 (comment 6109845672) have two fails, now with the builder:
1. **1 `notInserted` out of 48** scripted Dictations (`9E659272`). Explain the cause (a legitimate late-text hold, such as focus moved or typing since fn-up, or a bug) or fix it.
2. **Idle memory 36 MB** 11.5 minutes after the last Dictation, against the 30 MB bar (67 MB at 7.5 minutes). No model unload line appears in the log. Show whether the 10-minute unload fired and how much the open History window accounts for, then re-measure.

Everything else passes: launch to fn, offline (0 sockets), back to back, lone tap, quit and SIGTERM, crash recovery, and the bundle at 7.38 MB. The lag numbers (p50 159 ms, p95 351 ms) are provisional because of high load. My verdict stands otherwise: I merge once both are resolved on the head under review, with a Live checks re-check of whatever changes and green CI.

Refs #71

## Summary

A Lexicon page next to History, Import from a text file, and `lexicon-eval --lexicon <file>`. All three read one format, the one `scorer/testset` already reads: a bare line is a Term, `heard -> written` is a Rule, blank lines and `#` lines are skipped.

```diff
 menu bar menu
   History
+  Lexicon                     -> LexiconWindowPresenter.show()
 Lexicon page (LexiconUI/LexiconWindow.swift)
+  [Import…] [Add new]   [Search]
+  one list, Terms and Rules sorted together
+    gstack                                  [trash]
+    ✨ codecs → Codex   (✨ = learned)        [trash]
+  Add new: one field, one line of the file format (replaces that Term or heard side)
+  Import: NSOpenPanel -> LexiconFile -> Lexicon.add(entries) -> "Imported 6 Terms and 4 Rules"
 WordStore
+  LexiconFile(parsing:) / (contentsOf:)    # line-for-line parse_lexicon
+  Lexicon.add([LexiconEntry]) -> ImportCounts
+    one transaction, one recompile; an entry already there stays as it is
 lexicon-eval
+  --lexicon <file>   # file and manifest modes; each Dictation's temp Lexicon
+                     # manifest runs also pass the written forms as scorer --terms
```

Code Terms stay off the page (spec). One window at a time; closing drops it, like History.

## Evidence

- **Before:** no page, no import, `lexicon-eval --lexicon` is a usage error.
  **After:**
  - `LexiconImportTests` (10): parser cases mirror the scorer's. The Import button calls one store method, `Lexicon.add(contentsOf:)`, and the tests call the same one: the sample gives exactly its 6 Terms and 4 Rules (1 duplicate, 1 line not read); a second import gives `ImportCounts(terms: 0, rules: 0, duplicates: 11, unreadable: 1)` and an unchanged store; a missing file adds nothing; an import never overwrites an existing entry; it survives a reopen; imported Rules and folding apply at fn-down.
  - `LexiconTextTests` (16): row titles (`heard → written`, ✨ on learned only), search, sort, the Add field (a Term, a Rule typed with `->` or `→`, nothing else), import summary wording.
  - `EvalManifestTests` (+6): with the sample, a manifest run types "Frobnicate the QuuxKit.", without it "Frob nicate the quux kit."; the file is read by path; its written forms go to the scorer once each; `--lexicon` is refused with `--transcribe` and `--install-model`; an unreadable file fails before any Dictation; a run with a private Lexicon never goes in a git tree.
  - Scorer: a test pins `parse_lexicon` on the same sample the Swift tests read.
  - `scripts/check.sh` on 7059060: green. On c7c7210 (main merged, Import routed through `add(contentsOf:)`): 362 of 367 Swift tests pass; the 5 that fail are CodeTerms' real-FSEvents tests, which fail the same way at 7059060 on this machine now (load average about 8), so it's the machine; the scorer tests and the fixture eval pass. CI is the gate. Earlier, at 7059060: 341 Swift tests, 131 scorer tests, the import check, and the fixture eval (`--split everyday`, no `--lexicon`) at wer 0.0 and term_error_rate 0.0, unchanged. An earlier run failed `JevClientTests.pastTheBudgetTheFallbackDecides` (50 ms wall-clock budget, machine under load; Jev untouched); it passed alone and in the green run.
- **Scores:** no Test set scores. The Test set can't be scored until Jake reviews its gold (#51's page). Without `--lexicon` the eval pipeline is unchanged (same empty Lexicon, no `--terms`); the check script's fixture run is in the line above.
- **Live checks** at 7059060 ([comment](https://github.com/jparker2006/lexicon/issues/71#issuecomment-6109949605)): pass on the menu line and one window, Import of the sample ("Imported 6 Terms and 4 Rules", 10 rows), Add a Term and a Rule (`->` and `→`), bad input kept in the sheet, search (either side, any case, "No matches"), delete by button and by key, and rows kept across close and relaunch (footprint 34 MB closed, 35 open, 34 closed). Not run live: the second Import (the harness couldn't drive a second open panel; `importingTwiceCreatesNoDuplicates` covers it headless through the button's own store call) and the starter import, which waits for the daily-app install step below.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way. No schema change; Import and Add write rows to the existing `lexicon.sqlite`, and Delete on the page removes them.

**Blast Radius:** small.

Until #56, the app shell opens its own `Lexicon` just after launch, off the main thread (no launch cost before the fn tap), and the menu line appears once it is open (docs/architecture.md, Implementation reconciliation; `TODO(#56)`). `LexiconUI`, `LexiconApp` and `lexicon-eval` now depend on `WordStore` (architecture table updated for LexiconUI). History's hidden main menu moved to `KeyEquivalents.swift`, shared by both windows.

**Merge order with #129:** whichever lands second wires `LexiconWindowPresenter(lexicon: system.lexicon)` (store it as `public let lexicon` on `LexiconSystem`), deletes the shell's `Task` that opens a Lexicon and the `import WordStore` in AppDelegate. If #129 merges first I'll do it here. Expect small conflicts in AppDelegate.swift, LexiconEval/main.swift and architecture.md.

`--lexicon` also hands the scorer the Lexicon's written forms as `--terms`, which the scorer documents as "the whole Lexicon": false alarms and Term refs then count every Lexicon word, so a `--lexicon` run's Term scores aren't comparable to a run without it. The baseline is scored with the same list.

**Later:**
- `COLLATE NOCASE` (#70's schema) folds ASCII only: `Émile` and `émile` are two Terms, and RuleSet keeps one. Needs a migration with a stored folded key. Verified with sqlite3.
- eval's temp Lexicon, run file and `--terms` file are removed by `defer`, not on a signal (the run file's pattern predates this PR). They sit in the per-user temp folder.
- After #56, a page edit or Import rereads the system word list on the Lexicon actor (about 10 ms), so an fn-down at that moment waits for it.

## Install

Jake chose to import the starter Lexicon into the daily copy at install (recorded on #71). Run, in this order, from main:

```bash
scripts/import-lexicon.sh daily "$HOME/Library/Application Support/Lexicon/starter-lexicon.txt"
scripts/install.sh
```

The first prints counts only, expected `lexicon-eval: imported 45 Terms and 26 Rules; 0 already in the Lexicon; 0 lines not read`. It runs before the install because the app reads its Lexicon at launch. Safe to re-run: a second run imports nothing.

Check: open Lexicon from the menu bar, search for one of your Terms, and add one Rule with Add new.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

comments.body:
**Reviewer verdict: merge with notes** (head 599ed51)

Reviewed against review.md: the import parser, the store's import transaction, the page, the eval's `--lexicon`, and privacy. A critic covered everything through 7059060. I read the merge of main (051f823 keeps #127's `cloud: CloudLink = .network` beside the shared Lexicon) and c7c7210 (Import is now one store call, `Lexicon.add(contentsOf:)`, which reads the file on the Lexicon actor, off the main thread), and 599ed51 (`lexicon-eval --import-lexicon <file> --into <folder>` and `scripts/import-lexicon.sh dev|daily <file>`: the same store call, printing counts only, re-run safe, with a test).

What holds:
- Import is one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction with rollback. Parse errors happen before any write. A second import adds nothing, and existing entries are left as they were. The button and the tests now go through the same call, which covers Live checks item 3.
- The parser matches the scorer's `parse_lexicon` for comments, blank lines, splitting at the first arrow, empty sides and NFC.
- No SQLite or word-list read on the main thread.
- Logs and `scorer report` print counts only. The temp Lexicon and the `--terms` file are deleted when done. The fixture words are made up.
- Live checks passed items 1, 2 and 4 to 9. The footprint was 34 to 35 MB.

Notes, not blocking (copied to the Later comment on #36):
- A file line `codecs → Codex` imports as a Term holding the arrow. The Add field treats `→` as `->`, but `LexiconFile` and `parse_lexicon` don't. The page draws it like a Rule, and dictation never applies it. Accept `→` in both parsers, or count the line as not read.
- A Term that contains `->` (`p->next`) becomes the Rule "p" to "next". Rules match whole words in any case, so "plan p" would dictate as "plan next". The alert shows only the counts. Name new Rules' heard sides in the alert, or warn on a one-letter heard side.
- If `reload()` throws after COMMIT, the alert says "Nothing was added" though the rows were saved. Only on a read failure.
- Delete removes a row at once, with no undo. A learned Rule is gone unless it is imported again.

Starter import: per Jake's decision on #71, I run `scripts/import-lexicon.sh daily <starter path>` before `scripts/install.sh` on his next "install", reporting counts only.

Wire the live Dictation: fn-down starts capture and the History row, loads the local model if needed and holds a latency-critical activity; fn-up runs the adaptive tail, local Parakeet, rules-only Cleanup, queues text-ready, and pastes.
